content:
Aditya Rao: hey folks — Optimize question on SCM API. for what-if, we’re evaluating a bunch of candidate configs (batching/caching/quant profile) per workload. do we have/plan a multi-scenario endpoint so we can send N scenarios in one call?

Hassan Mirza: ^ today we’re doing sequential calls to `/v1/cost-model/estimate` and it’s slow + noisy. typical sweep is 40–120 scenarios for one “recommendation”.

Priya Natarajan: we don’t have a multi-scenario endpoint in v1 right now. concern is request size + per-request latency variance + making retries messy.

Ethan Park: +1. also determinism & audit logging get trickier if we accept a mega payload. we can do it, but we need limits + clear error behavior.

Yara Haddad: we’re mostly repeating the same base inputs and only changing 2–3 fields per scenario (e.g. `batching.enabled`, `kv_cache.mode`, `quant_profile_id`). if we have to do 100 separate requests, the overhead dominates.

Jordan Lee: can you quantify what “overhead” looks like? are you hitting p95 latency budgets or just overall wall clock?

Hassan Mirza: wall clock. p95 single estimate is ~45–70ms in staging when warm. but 100* that + retries means a couple seconds, and in our pipeline we do this per route/model candidate.

Priya Natarajan: ok. for v1, can we start with client-side batching (concurrency + small batch sizes) instead of a new endpoint? e.g. send 10–20 concurrent calls, cap total.

Aditya Rao: we can, but we’ll likely trip rate limits / add load spikes. also would love the service to share common resolution (model catalog lookup, sku resolution) across scenarios.

Amara Diallo: from gateway perspective, a dedicated batch endpoint is doable but we need strict limits. otherwise we’ll see big payloads, timeouts, and retries amplifying.

Benji Okafor: also rollout-wise, a new endpoint means more surface area to feature flag + canary, plus docs + SDK updates.

Yara Haddad: what about a “batch” endpoint with hard caps? e.g. max 25 scenarios, each scenario is just “overrides” relative to base.

Ethan Park: “base + overrides” is attractive, but it’s basically a new schema. we need to make sure we don’t end up with ambiguous merges. also version negotiation becomes more complex.

Jordan Lee: simplest shape is `requests: []` where each entry is the same as a normal estimate request. no merge semantics. server just processes them in parallel and returns `responses: []` aligned by index.

Priya Natarajan: that’s simpler, but then you don’t get de-dupe of shared fields.

Hassan Mirza: we’d still take it if it’s 1 HTTP call. the main goal is reduce RPC overhead + make it easier to handle partial failures.

Amara Diallo: if we do batch, we should define:
- max scenarios per request (e.g. 25)
- max payload size (e.g. 256KB)
- per-item validation errors returned per-item (not fail whole batch)
- overall request returns 200 if at least 1 item processed? or always 200 with per-item status?

Ethan Park: careful: our API conventions usually avoid “200 with errors”. we can do `207 Multi-Status` or `200` with explicit per-item `status_code` fields (but that implies a response schema w/ status codes).

Jordan Lee: 207 might break some of our client plumbing. but we can keep HTTP 200 and have each item include `ok`/`error_code` etc. (still deterministic). i know that violates “no embedded status codes” a bit.

Priya Natarajan: another option: keep HTTP status for “batch-level” issues only (too large, invalid auth, unsupported version). then within payload return `results[]` where invalid items have `error` populated. i’m ok with that for internal use if we document.

Benji Okafor: internal-only + behind a feature flag would make this less scary. Optimize can be first client.

Aditya Rao: internal-only is fine for now. Optimize service is internal. we just need something stable-ish.

Hassan Mirza: also please include a server-side limit on total “compute cost” so someone can’t submit 25 huge seq_len scenarios and blow p99.

Ethan Park: yup. we can bound based on inputs: `max_total_tokens = sum(input_tokens + output_tokens)` across batch, reject with `SCM_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Jordan Lee: + enforce `max_batch_wall_time` (like 500ms) and fail remaining items? but then determinism/partial results semantics get weird.

Priya Natarajan: for v1.0, i’d rather hard reject if expected work exceeds threshold. no partial time-based cutoffs.

Amara Diallo: gateway can also enforce request timeout. but service should aim to complete under our normal budget.

Yara Haddad: what are you thinking on limits? 25 scenarios works. typical scenario payload is small.

Priya Natarajan: proposal:
- new endpoint: `POST /v1/cost-model/estimate:batch`
- request: `{ "items": [<EstimateRequest>...] }`
- response: `{ "items": [<EstimateResponse or Error>...] }` aligned by index
- limits: `items <= 25`, payload <= 256KB, sum(tokens) <= 2M (tbd)
- if any item invalid, only that item returns `error` object; batch returns 200
- if batch invalid (too many items, bad version header), return normal HTTP error

Jordan Lee: + version negotiation should be same as single endpoint (i.e. headers). batch endpoint supports same versions.

Benji Okafor: and we’ll put it behind `scm_batch_endpoint_enabled` flag in service + allowlist Optimize tenant/service principal.

Aditya Rao: sounds good. can we get an ETA / do we file a ticket?

Priya Natarajan: please file an ENG ticket under platform, link this thread. @Hassan Mirza / @Yara Haddad include your target limits + concurrency assumptions. we’ll start with “same request schema repeated” (no base+overrides) to ship faster.

Hassan Mirza: will do. thanks all.

Amara Diallo: :thumbsup: once ticket is up, loop me in for gateway config + max body size.

Ethan Park: and loop @Jordan Lee for response schema + compatibility notes.

Aditya Rao: ack — filing now.
